target.projectDescription: Command-line video downloader: a CLI tool (optparse, not argparse) that fetches webpages/JSON APIs/manifests from ~1000 site extractors through a networking layer (RequestDirector + urllib request handlers), downloads media via fragment/http/hls/external-downloaders, post-processes with ffmpeg-family postprocessors, and self-updates from GitHub releases. Attackers control: remote page/API/manifest content, response headers, websocket frames, CLI options, config files, environment variables, cookies/netrc credentials.

framework.notes: No web framework detected. All framework scores are below the 0.50 threshold, so no framework reference is loaded. yt-dlp is a CLI tool: entry point yt_dlp/__init__.py main() -> _real_main(argv) with optparse option parsing (yt_dlp/options.py:153 _YoutubeDLOptionParser(optparse.OptionParser)); the HTTP stack is its own yt_dlp/networking/ layer (RequestDirector over urllib request handlers), not a framework. inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attackers face (1) the network: every remote fetch goes through YoutubeDL.urlopen/RequestDirector; response bodies are read via urlh.read() and decoded (json.loads via _parse_json / direct sites, regex extraction, base64/zlib, m3u8/MPD/ISM manifests, websocket frames); (2) the CLI/config layer: optparse options (including --exec, --netrc-cmd, --sponskrub-args, external downloader args), config files shlex-split to argv level, batch files, environment variables; (3) credentials: netrc (including a --netrc-cmd shell command), browser cookie stores; (4) disk artifacts written from remote data and re-read (fragments, .ytdl state, write_pages dumps, info.json, cookies); (5) the update feed (GitHub API JSON, _update_spec, SHA2-256SUMS, release binaries). Process execution sinks are dominated by the internal yt_dlp.utils.Popen wrapper; exactly three shell=True string-command sites exist (ExecPP --exec, --netrc-cmd, and the Windows updater delayed-delete).

sinkFamilies.evidence: no os.system / os.popen / os.exec* / os.spawn* / pexpect / pty.spawn call exists anywhere in the tree (only pty.openpty at YoutubeDL.py:657 and a function-local 'import pty'); the query keeps these API families because they are the standard CWE-78 sink set and the candidate extraction is meant to be exhaustive

sanitizerObservations: exec.py:24 quotes only the legacy {} filepath placeholder with compat_shlex_quote; outtmpl-substituted fields are quoted only when the template uses the %(field)q conversion (escape_outtmpl), otherwise they land unquoted in the shell command string
extractor/common.py:1309 inserts netrc_machine into the --netrc-cmd shell string with a bare str.replace - no quoting
update.py:376 wraps old_filename in double quotes inside the cmd.exe string (program-controlled path, not attacker-controlled)
all non-shell execution sites use argv lists (Popen.run(cmd_list) / Popen(args_list) / subprocess.call(args)); sponskrub.py:81 splits user --sponskrub-args with shlex.split instead of a shell string
options.py:314-315 CLI alias callback uses shlex.split(opts.format(*map(shlex.quote, value))) - quoting applied before argv injection
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: The --exec/--exec-before-download postprocessor, --netrc-cmd, --sponskrub-args, --ffmpeg-args/--postprocessor-args and external-downloader arguments are documented user-facing features that intentionally run commands the user configures; the version probes (ffmpeg --version, git rev-parse), keyring queries and the bidiv/fribidi output workaround execute static or program-derived commands. These are recorded as sink candidates only, not as vulnerabilities; the candidate extraction deliberately does not presume exploitability of any site.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query compile followed by codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) and codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF. Per operator instruction, execution is deferred to a later step - this step generates the queries only.
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules (json/os/urllib/subprocess) or the internal yt_dlp.utils module
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver name); catches dynamic or unresolved shapes that API graphs miss and is subject to name-collision noise. The dominant sink in this codebase (bare Popen / Popen.run from-imported from yt_dlp.utils through relative imports) and the factory-generated _download_json boundary rely on ast matching

exclusions: no rows are filtered out of the raw extraction; test/ and devscripts/ call sites (test/test_execution.py, test/test_overwrites.py, test/test_verbose_output.py, devscripts/utils.py, devscripts/generate_aes_testdata.py, setup.py) are included and are identifiable by their file path for later FP filtering

pure logging/reporting helpers (to_screen, write_debug, report_warning) are not extracted as candidates; the ffmpeg.py:362 write_debug('ffmpeg command line: %s' % shell_quote(cmd)) display string is a logging site, not a sink

uncoveredCases: yt_dlp/extractor/common.py:1021-1091 __create_download_methods generates _download_json/_download_webpage/_download_xml (+_handle variants) at runtime and dispatches them through getattr (common.py:1069 'getattr(self, download_handle.__name__)(...)'). The generated methods have no static definition, so API graphs cannot bind self._download_json call targets; the query matches those boundaries purely on the member name (ast). Only the explicit overrides (crackle.py:70, eagleplatform.py:109, soundcloud.py:92, udemy.py:144, postprocessor/common.py:201) produce definition rows.

yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py:838 'super().__init__(*args, env=env, ...)' inside Popen.__init__ - the actual subprocess.Popen construction goes through the super() indirection and is not a syntactic exec call; mitigated by the internal_exec_wrapper rows for the Popen class (family 6b, class node) and the run() classmethod, plus the api/ast rows on every Popen(...)/Popen.run(...) call site.
Popen.run (:852-857) constructs the process via the dynamic 'cls(*args, **kwargs)' call - not a syntactic exec site; special-cased as an internal_exec_wrapper row on repo evidence.

Augmented assignments building command argv ('cmd += [...]', 'args += [...]') in downloader/external.py _make_cmd variants (e.g. CurlFD :222-238 'cmd += ["--header", f"{key}: {val}"]', FFmpegFD :578 'args += self._configuration_args(...) + ["-i", fmt["url"]]') are not represented by BinaryExpr nodes and are not captured as cmd_build rows; the consuming exec sites (_call_process, Popen at external.py:193/395/625) and their wrapper functions are captured.

yt_dlp/update.py:376 f-string command construction (f'ping 127.0.0.1 ... del /F "{old_filename}"') - f-string AST nodes are not directly matched; the call site is captured through its shell_true and indirect_exec rows.

downloader/websocket.py:48-53 - remote websocket data is written into an ffmpeg process stdin (sink.write at :53) rather than passed as argv; captured as a socket_recv source, but the stdin-to-process data flow is a Phase 2 modeling concern (MySummaries), not an extraction row.

Bare-name (from-import) execution sinks are only matched for distinctive names (system, popen, getoutput, getstatusoutput); bare call/run/check_call are too collision-prone. In this repository every subprocess site is attribute-qualified (subprocess.call in exec.py/rtsp.py, subprocess.run in devscripts) or goes through the Popen wrapper, so this gap is not exercised.

The relative from-import shape 'from ..utils import Popen' may not resolve through API::moduleImport("yt_dlp.utils"); family 3 (api) may therefore produce zero or few rows. The ast family (bare Popen(...) / Popen.run(...) name shapes) guarantees full coverage of those sites - the two families are intentionally redundant.

'.read()' is matched generically (any receiver): network response reads, file reads and stream reads are not distinguished syntactically; the flow_kind is a single 'read' and disambiguation is left to labeling.

The networking Response class in this snapshot has no .json() method (networking-rewrite era, verified: no 'def json(' in the tree); urllib.request.urlopen is kept in the decode/fetch API set but the project routes fetches through YoutubeDL.urlopen instead.

yt_dlp/jsinterp.py interprets remote JavaScript in-process (youtube.py:3043-3143 player JS) - that is the code-injection domain (pass 4), not command execution, so no candidate family is emitted for it here.

yt_dlp/update.py:203 're.match(pattern, identifier)' runs a REMOTE regex (_update_spec fetched from the update feed) against a local string - a regex-injection surface noted for awareness; it is not a CWE-78 command execution sink.

self.params.get(...) reads inside YoutubeDL.py are not matched (receiver chain 'self.params' is collision-prone across 1143 modules); the get_param accessor family covers the consumer-facing boundary actually used by the netrc/exec command paths.
